### poiseuille3dEoc

The examples `poiseuille2dEoc` and `poiseuille3dEoc` are extensions of the `poiseuille2d` and `poiseuille3d` examples, respectively, focusing on the experimental order of convergence (EOC) of the simulation.

The implementations therein run the Poiseuille flow simulations multiple times to subsequently analyze the different error norms of the simulations with an automated `gnuplot` output.
Exemplarily, the `poiseuille3dEoc` example is simulated for multiple configurations: the periodic pipe flow with *forcing* and several boundary methods at the walls (the keywords *interpolated*, *bouzidi*, and *bounce back* specify the implementations), as well as a bounded domain case where a *velocity inlet* and a *pressure outlet* are prescribed and combined with a *bouzidi* boundary at the pipe wall.
For all simulations, the Reynolds number of the flow problem is set to $Re = 10$ and the relaxation time to $\tau = 0.8$.
The EOC is investigated by running four consecutive simulations with increasing grid resolution (number of lattice cells along the pipe diameter: $N_D = 21, 31, 41, 51$).
A residual below 1e-5 stops each simulation via the convergence criteria.
The absolute error of the simulation from the analytic solution is evaluated on every lattice node whereby different norms for the error calculation are used.
The $L_1$-norm is defined as

$$
E_{\mathrm{abs}, L_1} = \sum^{N}_i \sum^D_d|\phi_{\mathrm{sim},i,d} - \phi_{\mathrm{ana},i,d}|\,\triangle x^D ~,
$$

where $N$ is the number of lattice nodes, $D$ is the number of dimensions of the variable $\phi$, $\phi_{\mathrm{sim}}$ is the solution of a flow variable obtained by the simulation, $\phi_{\mathrm{ana}}$ is the corresponding analytic solution, and $\triangle x$ is the grid spacing.
The $L_2$-norm is defined as

$$
E_{\mathrm{abs}, L_2} = \sqrt{\sum^{N}_i \sum^D_d|\phi_{\mathrm{sim},i,d} - \phi_{\mathrm{ana},i,d}|^2 \,\triangle x^D} ~.
$$

Finally, the $L_\infty$-norm is defined as

$$
E_{\mathrm{abs}, L_\infty} = \max_{i,d}|\phi_{\mathrm{sim},i,d} - \phi_{\mathrm{ana},i,d}| ~.
$$

The relative error according to the $L_1$-norm is defined as

$$
E_{\mathrm{rel}, L_1} = \frac{E_{\mathrm{abs}, L_1}}{\sum^{N}_i \sum^D_d|\phi_{\mathrm{ana},i,d}|\,\triangle x^D} ~,
$$

the $L_2$-norm as

$$
E_{\mathrm{rel}, L_2} = \frac{E_{\mathrm{abs}, L_2}}{\sqrt{\sum^{N}_i \sum^D_d|\phi_{\mathrm{ana},i,d}|^2\,\triangle x^D}} ~,
$$

and the $L_\infty$-norm as

$$
E_{\mathrm{rel}, L_\infty} = \frac{E_{\mathrm{abs}, L_\infty}}{\max_{i,d}|\phi_{\mathrm{ana},i,d}|} ~.
$$

The results of the EOC tests are plotted in @fig-eocPoiseuille3d-interpol, @fig-eocPoiseuille3d-bouzidi, @fig-eocPoiseuille3d-bounceback, @fig-eocPoiseuille3d-inout-bouzidi and @fig-eocPoiseuille3d-pressure.
